title: Federated Graph Learning with Structure Proxy Alignment

problem.claim: Federated graph learning faces label-distribution heterogeneity across clients and biased neighboring information for minority-class nodes, impairing convergence and expressive node embeddings in node classification.

gap.claim: Existing federated graph learning approaches need a way to address divergent local objectives and biased neighboring information caused by heterogeneous graph data.

contributions.claim: FedSpray learns local class-wise structure proxies in latent space and aligns them into global structure proxies on the server.
FedSpray trains a global feature-structure encoder and uses structure proxies to generate unbiased soft targets for personalized local GNN training.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe FedSpray as a novel federated graph learning framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments were conducted on four datasets.
The authors report that FedSpray outperformed other baselines.
The authors report that their code is available online.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated graph learning trains graph learning models over graph data distributed across multiple owners.
Client label distributions can differ substantially, producing divergent local objectives and impairing convergence for node classification.
Minority-class nodes may have biased neighboring information, limiting expressive GNN node embeddings.
FedSpray aligns local class-wise latent structure proxies into global server-side proxies and uses them to support personalized local training.
The authors report experiments on four datasets showing superiority over baselines.

source_observation.claim: Client-specific label imbalance and biased local neighborhoods can create divergent objectives and unreliable structural signals in federated node classification.

interpretation.claim: Federated graph learning may benefit from globally aligned structural information that compensates for client-local distribution and neighborhood bias.

application.claim: Use aligned class-wise structure proxies and personalized soft-target regularization when designing federated node-classification systems with heterogeneous client graphs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported node-classification setting or four datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the alignment objective, model architecture details, or training procedure.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported superiority.
